A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CtrlHGen research work with complete main text and Appendices A–D. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the methods, equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on DBpedia50, WN18RR, and FB15k-237, including baseline comparisons, ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The sub-logic decomposition, conditional Transformer training, semantic and condition-adherence rewards, and GRPO procedure are identical in Section 3 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three datasets, thirteen logical patterns, five control conditions, and case-study scenarios, including the multi-round dialogue example.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1, 2, 4, 8, and 9, including AbductiveKGR, the LLM comparisons and RAG variant, Logic-Gen, and AbductiveKGR with condition tokens.

E3.justification: The data splits, evaluation metrics, model configuration, training budgets, prompting procedures, and temperature settings remain identical in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

E4.justification: Both versions retain identical decomposition and reward ablations, temperature sensitivity results, relation-count visualization, and structural, semantic, and dialogue case studies.

E5.justification: Mean and standard-deviation reporting is unchanged. Neither version adds or revises run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–9 and the plotted and qualitative results match, including the appendix ablations and case-study scores.

T1.justification: The open-world assumption, problem definition, mathematical formulations in Equations 1–8, and appendix algorithm descriptions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain identical claims about controllable abductive reasoning, the proposed components, and experimental advantages.

C2.justification: Interpretations of hypothesis-space collapse, reward sensitivity, LLM weaknesses, control-versus-semantics tradeoffs, and practical applicability remain unchanged, including Appendix C.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, sampling instructions, prompts, and the code-access statement are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgment provides no new technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Related-work discussion and cited works are identical. The Camposampiero and Pukancová references move across page boundaries but are neither added nor removed.

P1.justification: Section 6 adds the sentence acknowledging support from RGC JRFS2526-6S10, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added acknowledgment causes limited reference reflow across pages 11–13. Figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a funding credit in Section 6, updates the version stamp, and reflows references. The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information are identical, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
